name: Side Hustle Startup
description: A 90-minute, 4-round basic Express simulation on starting a one-person service business from zero, for high-school Career and Technical Education (business, marketing and landscape), entrepreneurship and personal-finance courses, career and technical student organizations and youth-entrepreneurship programs. Isaiah Varnadoe, 16, a fictional sophomore in Largo, Florida, mows his neighbors' lawns from 31 May to 19 September 2027, scored in four four-week periods. Round by round you set the price of a visit and choose the tools, choose how to find customers and how to keep the books, decide what to do when there are more customers than hours and which add-on to sell, and keep the business going when school starts while handling a customer's cracked glass door. Each period is scored on profit, profit per hour, weekly customers, reputation and records and compliance; flyers in mailboxes (18 U.S.C. 1725), or weed and feed applied for pay without the license Florida requires, caps the score. English with Spanish.
view:
Side Hustle Startup

One mower, one summer, one subdivision in Largo, Florida: four rounds of decisions, from the first time a neighbor asks what you charge to the second week of school.

Isaiah Varnadoe · lawn care · Largo, Florida · May to September 2027 You are Isaiah Varnadoe, 16, and you have just finished your sophomore year in Largo, Florida. You live with your mother, Vanessa, a respiratory therapist who works twelve-hour shifts, in the Bayhaven Oaks subdivision: about 300 homes on small lots of St. Augustine grass that needs cutting every week all summer. Three neighbors have already asked you to mow, among them Harold Tisdale, a retired mail carrier two doors down. Adult crews charge about $45 a visit for a small lot. You have $600 saved and about 30 hours a week in June and July; from Wednesday 11 August school takes the weekdays and you have about 12 hours a week. A visit — mow, edge, trim, blow — costs you $2.00 in gas, oil and line, plus travel at about $0.12 a minute, and Florida's minimum wage is $14 an hour. Each round is scored on its own four weeks: profit, profit per hour, weekly customers, reputation and records and compliance.

Round 1 — Saturday 29 May 2027: the price and the tools

Harold Tisdale asks what you charge, and you have no answer. A friend says $15 so nobody says no; your mother says to charge by the hour, like a job; a neighbor says the crews charge $45. A visit takes you about an hour with travel. At Gulfline Outdoor Power a salesperson shows a new mower, trimmer, blower and edger for $1,480 on your mother's store card, no interest if paid in full in 12 months; a seller on a local marketplace has a used self-propelled mower, trimmer and blower for $480, and you can test-start them first; the family's old push mower is in the garage; a rental store rents mowers and trimmers by the day.

Deliverable: your price and your tools. This round is scored on 31 May–27 June.

Round 2 — Monday 28 June 2027: the marketing and the books

Four weeks in, the lawns you have are the lawns that asked. Your mother offers to post on Nextdoor (its members must be 18), a printer quotes door hangers, she could run a paid social ad from her own account, and a friend says to put a flyer in every mailbox in three subdivisions — everybody does it. Your money is in your pocket, a notebook and a payment app on your personal account.

Deliverable: how you find customers and how you keep the money from 28 June. This round is scored on 28 June–25 July.

Round 3 — Monday 26 July 2027: more customers than hours, and the add-ons

The homeowners' association has sent courtesy notices about overgrown lawns and the phone has not stopped: about six more requests this period, more than your hours allow. School starts on Wednesday 11 August: 30 hours a week until then, about 12 after — 18 a week on average for these four weeks. Customers ask whether you do weed and feed; the hardware store sells it by the bag. Your friend Tre Gaskins, 16, wants in.

Deliverable: what you do when demand passes your hours, and the add-on from 26 July. This round is scored on 26 July–22 August.

Round 4 — Monday 23 August 2027: school and the cracked door

On Saturday 21 August, at 10:40 a.m., a rock thrown by your trimmer cracked Bernadette Quisenberry's sliding glass door; a glass company quotes $520. School is in its second week and you have about 12 hours a week. Wade Ricketson, owner of Ricketson Turf Pros, offers to take the lawns you cannot keep — or to buy your whole customer list.

Deliverable: the business in the school weeks and what you do about the door. This round is scored on 23 August–19 September.

summary.en: You are Isaiah Varnadoe, a 16-year-old high-school student in Largo, Florida, and you start mowing your neighbors' lawns for pay in the summer of 2027. You set the price of a visit, choose tools, find customers, keep the books and keep going once school starts.
summary.es: Eres Isaiah Varnadoe, estudiante de secundaria de 16 años en Largo, Florida, y empiezas a cortar el césped de tus vecinos a cambio de dinero en el verano de 2027. Fijas el precio de cada visita, eliges herramientas, buscas clientes, llevas las cuentas y sigues cuando empiezan las clases.

text.en: Build a price per visit from the time a job takes, its supplies, travel and tools and the value of the founder's hour, and check it against the customer's next-best option
text.es: Calcular un precio por visita a partir del tiempo que lleva el trabajo, sus insumos, el desplazamiento, las herramientas y el valor de la hora del fundador, y contrastarlo con la mejor alternativa del cliente

text.en: Keep a simple P&L that records every visit, invoice, expense and payment, spreads tool costs over the season and sets aside the self-employment tax owed on the profit
text.es: Llevar una cuenta de resultados sencilla que registre cada visita, factura, gasto y cobro, reparta el coste de las herramientas a lo largo de la temporada y reserve el impuesto de autónomo que se debe sobre el beneficio

text.en: Select a local or social marketing channel by the customers it reaches, the route it builds and its cost, while staying within the law and the platforms' rules
text.es: Seleccionar un canal de marketing local o en redes según los clientes que alcanza, la ruta que construye y su coste, sin salirse de la ley ni de las normas de las plataformas

text.en: Design a capacity plan for growing demand that uses a waitlist, a price for new demand, a partner on clear terms or a tighter route, and carries the business through the start of school
text.es: Diseñar un plan de capacidad para la demanda creciente que use una lista de espera, un precio para la nueva demanda, un socio con condiciones claras o una ruta más compacta, y mantenga el negocio al empezar el curso escolar

text.en: Judge which add-on services fit one's skills and licenses, own a mistake on a customer's property quickly and fully, and hand customers on without selling their details
text.es: Juzgar qué servicios adicionales encajan con las propias habilidades y licencias, asumir rápida y plenamente un error en la propiedad de un cliente y traspasar clientes sin vender sus datos
